meanings.note: Used in chamar a atenção (to catch someone's eye) and as an announcement call.

examples.text: Esse fio está me chamando a atenção.
examples.trans: This wire is catching my attention.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular.
Aparecer na frente means to show up in the lead in election tallies.

examples.trans: The candidate appears in the lead.
He showed up at the meeting.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Assumir a liderança means to take the lead.

examples.trans: She took over the new position.

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Assumir a liderança and voltar à liderança are standard election-night phrases for taking the lead.

examples.text: Ela voltou à liderança na pesquisa.
examples.trans: She returned to the lead in the poll.

meanings.note: First-person plural possessive agreeing in gender and number with the noun.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: In the exclamation Nossa Senhora! (Our Lady!), expresses shock or amazement.
Signature regional interjection of Minas Gerais expressing surprise, agreement, or obviousness.

examples.text: Uai, esse homem é bom demais!
examples.trans: Why, this man is way too good!
Well now, didn't you know that?

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

examples.text: Vou ficar sentado esse tempo inteiro.
examples.trans: I'm going to stay seated that whole time.

meanings.note: Adult male human; plural homens.
Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).
Placed after an adjective (bom demais), means so good / way too good.
Irregular past eu fiz (I made/did); não tem o que fazer means having nothing to do.

examples.text: Ela não tem o que fazer agora.
examples.trans: She has nothing to do now.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Diminutive of café (-zinho) naming Brazil's classic friendly coffee break.

examples.trans: Shall we grab a little coffee?
Would you like a quick coffee now?

meanings.note: Singular um pão in Brazil usually means a French bread roll.

examples.text: Só pra chegar e comprar um pão.
examples.trans: Just to get there and buy a roll of bread.
I bought fresh bread in the morning.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Spelled with a circumflex when stressed at the end of a phrase or alone (É o quê? / Por quê?).

virar.gloss: to turn the tables; overtake; turn

meanings.en: to turn the tables; overtake; turn
meanings.note: In sports and elections, virar (Lula virou!) means to come from behind and take the lead.

examples.text: O jogo virou no segundo tempo.
examples.trans: The game turned around in the second half.

examples.text: Lula virou na contagem dos votos.
examples.trans: Lula took the lead in the vote count.

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
With ir, ir embora means to leave or go away (here euphemistically for passing on).

examples.text: Mas tá indo embora na verdade.
examples.trans: But she is leaving in fact.

meanings.note: Informal reduced para. Before a feminine noun, this Brazilian spelling can also represent a contraction including the article a; the exact meeting is clear from context.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.
Everyday verb for washing hands, face, or clothes.

examples.trans: I am going to wash my hands.

meanings.note: Automobile; de carro means by car.

examples.text: A gente pegou o carro cedo.
Deixei o carro estacionado lá fora.
examples.trans: I left the car parked outside.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Arrumar a casa means to clean and tidy up the house.

examples.text: Você arruma a casa das pessoas.

examples.trans: I need to tidy up my desk.

meanings.note: Means both a house building and home.

examples.text: Vou voltar pra casa da minha mãe.
examples.trans: I am going to go back to my mother's house.

meanings.note: Plural as pessoas means people.
Alone as vocative gente! it means folks/guys; with article a gente it means we/us with third-person singular verbs.

examples.text: Você acha que é melhor que a gente?
examples.trans: Do you think you're better than us?
Oh, folks, the meeting ran late.

meanings.note: Used for ordering food or requesting an Uber.

examples.trans: I am going to order my ride now.

meanings.note: Points to someone or something further away from both speakers.

examples.text: Você tá vendo aquela moça ali?
examples.trans: Do you see that young woman over there?
That chart over there is great.

meanings.note: Informal second-person singular possessive, very common in Rio speech.

examples.trans: Your husband is already doing great.

meanings.note: Warm address among colleagues or ironical buddy in an argument.

examples.text: Ele é meu amigo do trabalho.
examples.trans: He is my friend from work.

meanings.note: In apposition (amigo pastor), describes a friend who is an evangelical pastor.

examples.trans: That friend of yours is a pastor.

examples.text: O pastor falou com a comunidade.
examples.trans: The pastor spoke with the community.

meanings.note: Points to a place away from the speaker; lá dentro reinforces inside there.
Frequentar uma igreja means to attend a church regularly.

examples.text: A gente devia frequentar uma igreja.

meanings.note: Third-person masculine singular subject pronoun.
Imperfect devia + infinitive is the everyday spoken way to say should (você devia apagar); present deve + infinitive expresses probability (ele deve ter).

examples.text: Ele deve ter sede lá em Orlando.
examples.trans: He must have a branch there in Orlando.

meanings.note: Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: With open [ɛ], means the headquarters or branch of a church, club, or company.

examples.text: A igreja tem sede em Orlando.
examples.trans: The church has a branch in Orlando.

examples.text: A sede da empresa fica em São Paulo.
examples.trans: The company's headquarters is in São Paulo.

meanings.note: Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.
Colocar a gente na comunidade means to get us into the community.

examples.text: Ele coloca a gente na comunidade.
examples.trans: He puts us into the community.
I placed the document on the table.

meanings.note: Refers to a local expat or church community.

examples.text: Ele coloca a gente na comunidade.
examples.trans: He puts us into the community.

examples.text: A comunidade brasileira lá é grande.
examples.trans: The Brazilian community there is large.

meanings.note: Acabou o seu tempo is the standard phrase for 'Your time is up.'
Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: One's life or daily existence.

examples.text: É isso que você quer pra sua vida?
examples.trans: Is that what you want for your life?

examples.text: A vida no escritório é corrida.

meanings.note: Expresses emotion, relief, or sudden pain.

examples.text: Ai, doutor! Como foi a cirurgia?
examples.trans: Oh, doctor! How did the surgery go?

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: Informal word for prison or jail.

examples.text: Eles pediram cadeia para o juiz.
examples.trans: They called for jail for the judge.

meanings.note: Time between midday and evening; boa tarde! greets or bids farewell in the afternoon.

examples.text: A reunião é hoje à tarde.
